# Hermes Agent — FAQ & Onboarding Guide

### 1. General & Setup

**How do I check system health and configuration?**
Run `hermes doctor` to verify Python version, virtual environment, dependencies, `.env`, `config.yaml`, and auth status.

**Is there a Web UI/Dashboard?**
Yes. Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`. It includes a browser-based chat tab with the embedded TUI.

**Which platforms and operating systems are supported?**
- **Linux & macOS:** Fully supported.
- **Windows:** Tier 1 support on Windows 10/11 via the native PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is recommended only if you need the web dashboard's embedded terminal pane (requires POSIX PTY).
- **Docker / NAS (UGOS, Synology, unRAID):** Official multi-arch Docker images (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) run natively on Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon. To avoid permission errors on host bind-mounts, supply `PUID=1000` and `PGID=10` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`).
- **Android / Termux:** Supported natively using the `termux-all` dependency bundle via `scripts/install.sh`.

**How do I report security vulnerabilities?**
Submit via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or email `security@nousresearch.com` per `SECURITY.md`.

---

### 2. Model Providers & Configuration

**Why is my local Ollama model slow?**
Small local models (e.g., 4B–9B) process large prompts slowly because Hermes sends ~45 tool schemas per call. To optimize:
- Disable unnecessary tools: `hermes tools`.
- Use faster quantization or switch to larger models (32B+).
- Set `terminal.backend: local` to eliminate container overhead.

**Why is my local endpoint (`base_url`) ignored?**
If `provider: auto` is set, Hermes prioritizes cloud API keys found in your environment (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Explicitly configure custom/local endpoints in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
model:
  default: ollama/<model_name>
  provider: custom
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
fallback_providers: []
```

**How do I connect other providers?**
- **Ollama Cloud:** Use `provider: ollama-cloud` (routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`).
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` (auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`) or set `provider: azure-foundry`.
- **Google Gemini:** OAuth inference methods are deprecated. Use Google AI Studio API keys via `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **Claude Pro/Max Subscriptions:** Using API keys incurs standard API token billing. To use Pro/Max subscription tiers, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Vision on Custom Endpoints:** Enable native image payloads on OpenAI-compatible models by setting `supports_vision: true` in your model config.
- **Local Token Usage:** OpenAI-compatible streaming automatically requests `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` to track tokens in `/usage`.

**Does Hermes support automatic cheap/smart model routing?**
No. Automatic complexity-based routing across model tiers is not supported. Hermes retains the session's primary model. For sub-agents, configure `delegation.provider` and `delegation.model` in `config.yaml`.

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways & Platforms

**How do I set up messaging gateways?**
Run the interactive wizard `hermes gateway setup` to configure Discord, Telegram, Slack, Matrix, etc.

**Why does Telegram show "Unauthorized user"?**
`allowed_chats` only filters group chat IDs. For DM user authorization, use one of:
- Allowlist user IDs: `telegram.allow_from: "<USER_ID>"` in `config.yaml`.
- Pair interactively: DM the bot, then run `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
- Allow all users: `telegram.allow_all: true`.

**Can gateways handle files and images?**
- **Inbound:** Discord, Telegram, and other gateways accept file uploads (including text and `.py` scripts) directly into agent context.
- **Outbound:** Generated local files and tool outputs are sent natively: Matrix (`m.file`), Email (SMTP attachments), Telegram (native images), and DingTalk (Markdown `![image](url)`). MCP tools emit `MEDIA:<path>` tags for automatic delivery.

**Can I run distinct personas per channel or multiple user accounts?**
- **Per-Channel Persona:** Set `channel_prompts` in your gateway platform config (supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost).
- **Multi-Account/Profile:** Hermes supports gateway multiplexing (`d5d02eabb`), enabling multiple isolated profiles/accounts on a single gateway instance.

---

### 4. Agent Core, Memory & Plugins

**How do I manage agent personality and user memory?**
- `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: System persona and identity.
- `~/.hermes/USER.md`: User-specific profiles, preferences, and facts (updated via memory tool `target="user"`).
- `MEMORY.md`: Long-term episodic memory.

**How does task continuation and turn limits work?**
The session turn limit defaults to 90 (`agent.max_turns` in config or `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For long-running tasks, use `/goal <task>` to persist tasks across turns and resume paused sessions with `/goal resume`. If an interrupted session resets, restore it with `/resume`.

**How do I create custom tools and memory backends?**
- **Custom Tools:** Create plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` using `ctx.register_tool(...)` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <name>`.
- **Memory Providers:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Implement the `MemoryProvider` ABC as a standalone plugin in `~/.hermes/plugins/` or publish via pip.
- **Observability:** Enable Langfuse tracing via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Skill Usage Tracking:** Inspect skill execution metrics via `/insights`, `hermes insights`, or `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`.
